findings.reason: a worker implementing only the named sites fails two of six cases and one of seven controls, and the plan must name the covering-set enumeration in `crew_dispatch_commands.py` as a change site so the mechanism is stated where the work is.
findings.text: the Deliverable names only two mechanism sites (the `max` tie fixes) plus "the refusal remains only when two covering reviews cannot be ordered, but the covering set in `crew review --answer` is built at `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:2761-2775` from exactly two candidates, `(record, design)`, where `record = read_plan_review(...)` is a single content review (`:2731`); fixing both `max` sites leaves the covering list capped at one content review, so case 3 (naming the older review with `--review-run` is written there) still refuses, and case 6 (two covering reviews, one untimestamped, refused naming both) can never assemble two entries and its negative control "deleting the ambiguity refusal outright answers the sixth case" cannot fail

findings.reason: the plan's write paths reach the right file but its mechanism names the wrong gate, and a worker following the sentence literally writes a parameter that never arrives at the answer verb.
findings.text: the MCP half of the Deliverable says `review_run` is added to `_crew`'s signature and "passed through its `_crew_write_action` call", but `_crew_write_action` forwards kwargs verbatim (`reckon/mcp.py:2919-2921`) to `crew_action`, which dispatches through the per-action argument map in `reckon/mcp_crew_actions.py`; the `"answer"` map there (`reckon/mcp_crew_actions.py:135-143`) lists `project`, `plan`, `finding`, `acted`, `note`, `declined`, `session` and no `review_run`, so a signature parameter alone is dropped and case 4 cannot pass
